newsitem.title: GERMANY: INSTANT VIEW - German industry output up in July.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - German industry output up in July.

text.p: Following are analysts' reactions to the economics ministry's announcement that German industrial output rose 0.2 percent in July from the previous month, slowing from 0.7 percent growth in June.
Output was down 1.6 percent from July 1995, compared with a 0.8 percent year-on-year decline in June, according to Reuters calculations based on Bundesbank statistics.
Average market expectations were for slightly stronger figures, a 0.4 percent rise in output from the previous month, and a 1.3 percent decline from the year-earlier month. @
Holger Schmieding, Merrill Lynch in Frankfurt:
"It is close to consensus and is the fifth monthly rise in a row which is unusual and does confirm that the economy is in a nice uptrend."
"July was 0.9 percent over the average of Q2. If output remains only steady from now on, it will give quite reasonable third quarter GDP growth."
"West German manufacturing is doing well which fits in with the latest, very strong, Ifo report for July."
Norbert Braems, Barclays de Zoete Wedd, Frankfurt:
"These numbers are a little disappointing, and contradict what we see in other indicators.
"We believed the numbers should be higher, after the Ifo institute said July numbers should be better. The car sector was strong in July.
"These data are preliminary, and there may be some revisions. Particularly east Germany looks not very good. Ifo was very strong on the current production level.
